QUESTION:
Which other drugs interact with Prednisone?

RESPONSE:
Short answer: the label excerpt you've given me only contains the INDICATIONS and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION sections for prednisone tablets — it does not include a Drug Interactions section, so I can't quote specific interaction information from it.

What the excerpt does mention that is interaction-adjacent:
• Prednisone is used together with mineralocorticoids in adrenocortical insufficiency (especially in infancy).
• In fulminating/disseminated pulmonary tuberculosis and in tuberculous meningitis, it is to be used only concurrently with appropriate antituberculous chemotherapy.

For general awareness (not from this excerpt — please verify against the full prescribing information), corticosteroids such as prednisone are commonly reported to interact with:
• CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenytoin, phenobarbital, carbamazepine) — may reduce prednisone effect
• CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, grapefruit) — may increase corticosteroid exposure/effects
• NSAIDs and aspirin — increased risk of GI ulceration/bleeding
• Anticoagulants such as warfarin — altered anticoagulant response (monitor INR)
• Potassium-depleting agents (loop/thiazide diuretics, amphotericin B) — hypokalemia
• Antidiabetic drugs and insulin — reduced glycemic control; doses may need adjustment
• Live or live-attenuated vaccines — should generally be avoided at immunosuppressive doses; vaccine response may be diminished
• Other immunosuppressants — additive infection risk
• Cholinesterase inhibitors (e.g., in myasthenia gravis) — risk of severe weakness
• Isoniazid, cyclosporine, digitalis glycosides, oral contraceptives/estrogens, quinolone antibiotics (tendon rupture risk)

Because the excerpt provided doesn't cover interactions, please consult the complete FDA-approved prescribing information for this specific product, or ask a pharmacist or prescriber, and give them your full medication, supplement, and vaccine history before starting or changing prednisone.
